meta.scope: Peru batch 4 — Coffee & agriculture (Andean/highland production), additional trade agreements (US, China), and supporting Andean/regional anchors. Final expansion pass.

candidates.title: Café — producción y exportaciones
candidates.publisher: MIDAGRI / Junta Nacional del Café / SUNAT / INEI
candidates.description: Statistics of coffee production and exports. Leading traditional agricultural export, produced mainly by smallholders in Andean and Amazonian foothill regions. Peru is a major organic-coffee exporter.
candidates.notes: Signature soft-commodity export. 2025 exports reached record levels (reports in the USD 1.7–1.8 bn range). Produced in 16 regions; main producers include San Martín, Cajamarca, Junín, Cusco and Amazonas. Continuously cited in agro-export and rural-economy analysis.

candidates.title: Agroexportaciones / Non-traditional agricultural exports
candidates.description: Broader statistics of agricultural and agro-industrial exports (fresh produce, processed foods, coffee, cocoa, etc.). Complements the mining-dominated traditional-export basket.
candidates.notes: Non-traditional agro-exports have been a diversification success story. Coffee is the largest single traditional agricultural line; blueberries, grapes, avocados and asparagus are major non-traditional lines.

candidates.title: Tratado de Libre Comercio Perú–Estados Unidos
candidates.description: Bilateral free-trade agreement in force since February 2009. Core preferential-access instrument for the US market and a recurring reference in trade and investment analysis.
referenced_by: Export statistics by partner (US is a top destination for coffee and other agro-exports)
Policy debates on market access and diversification
candidates.notes: Major bilateral FTA. Continuously cited in official trade-performance reporting. Nearly all Peruvian tariff lines enter the US duty-free under the agreement.

candidates.title: Tratado de Libre Comercio Perú–China
candidates.publisher: Gobierno del Perú / República Popular China
candidates.description: Bilateral free-trade agreement in force since March 2010. Underpins the large and growing bilateral trade relationship, especially mining and agricultural exports to China.
referenced_by: Official monitoring of the China FTA
candidates.notes: Structurally important bilateral instrument. China is a top destination for Peruvian copper and other minerals; the FTA is routinely cited in explanations of the trade relationship.

candidates.title: Sierra — natural-region statistical domain
candidates.description: Andean highlands natural region used as a standard geographic domain in ENAHO poverty and living-conditions analysis. Highest rural poverty incidence.
candidates.notes: Key natural-region domain. Sierra rural recorded the highest monetary poverty in 2025 (~38.8%). Hosts much of the coffee and highland agricultural production as well as important mining districts.

candidates.title: Selva — natural-region statistical domain
candidates.description: Amazonian natural region used as a standard geographic domain in ENAHO analysis. Elevated rural poverty and important coffee/cocoa producing zones.
candidates.notes: Selva rural poverty remains elevated (~30.7% in 2025). Contains major coffee-producing departments such as San Martín and parts of Amazonas.

candidates.title: Costa — natural-region statistical domain
candidates.description: Coastal natural region used as a standard geographic domain. Lowest poverty incidence among the three natural regions; hosts the capital and the bulk of non-traditional agro-exports.
candidates.notes: Costa urbana has the lowest poverty rates. Completes the three natural-region domains (Costa–Sierra–Selva) that structure much of Peruvian social and agricultural analysis.

candidates.title: Departamento de San Martín — coffee-producing Andean–Amazon transition
candidates.description: Major coffee-producing department in the Andean–Amazon transition zone. Important for both agricultural-export and rural-poverty analysis.
candidates.notes: One of the leading coffee regions. Links the commodity (coffee) to the departmental and natural-region poverty/production geography.

candidates.title: Canon minero y regalías mineras
candidates.publisher: MEF / Ministerio de Energía y Minas
candidates.description: Mining canon and royalty transfers from central government to producing regions and local governments. Major sub-national fiscal mechanism linking mining production to territorial budgets.
candidates.notes: Critical sub-national fiscal node. Directly links the mining production and export statistics to departmental and municipal budgets, especially in the Sierra and mining corridors.

candidates.title: Departamento de Moquegua — low-poverty mining contrast
candidates.description: Southern mining department with very low monetary-poverty incidence. Completes the mining-department contrast alongside Ica.
candidates.notes: 2025 monetary poverty ~7.8%. Hosts major copper operations; illustrates that mining presence can coincide with low measured poverty under the national framework.

proposed_edges.basis: Coffee is a major traditional agricultural export line.
Coffee is the leading traditional agricultural component of agro-exports.
The US FTA underpins preferential bilateral trade flows, including coffee and other agro-exports.
The China FTA underpins the large bilateral trade relationship, especially minerals.
Sierra is a standard natural-region domain in the poverty analysis.
Canon and royalties are generated by mining production.
San Martín is one of the principal coffee-producing departments.
